audit_scope: full-corpus read-only replay of the project-declared legacy donor table; 3,601 complete reaction SMILES checked against reacting-center fragment-pair evidence

categories.cross_lineage_pair: Legacy transformed_pair picked a (X, Y) pair that crosses independent lineages — e.g. pairing 2-oxoglutarate -> hydroxyproline instead of proline -> hydroxyproline. This is the §9.3 forbidden-lineage failure mode: legacy single-pair selection cannot represent two parallel transformed lineages in one reaction.
categories.cofactor_selected_as_main: Legacy pick_main (or _pick_transformed with an empty reaction-center fallback) selected a conserved cofactor (NADH/CoA/ATP/FAD/...) as the main substrate or product, mislabeling a spectator as the transformed core. COFACTORS stripping mitigates this only when the cofactor SMILES exactly matches the frozenset entry.
categories.mapping_missing: No verifiable atom mapping exists for the reaction — either rdkit cannot parse it, chenyu_features.reaction_center_from_chenyu returned None, or the mapper backend is absent. Without a map there is no formal atom-transfer evidence, so the legacy pair is unsupported.
categories.legacy_pair_supported: The legacy transformed_pair (X, Y) IS supported by the available mapping/lineage evidence — X and Y are the true transformed core and the pair does not cross lineages. This is the agreement category.
categories.insufficient_evidence: Evidence is too thin to classify the legacy pair as either supported or a mismatch — e.g. ambiguous reaction center, partial mapping, or missing source stoichiometry. The record is retained (not deleted) and flagged for downstream quarantine/diagnostic review.

source_authority.name: chenyu_formal_filtered_train_positive_cache
source_authority.limitation: Auditable as the legacy donor corpus; not represented as a RHEA/BRENDA/MetaCyc export.

legacy_logic_risks.risk: Selects a single 'largest fragment' by (heavy_atoms, carbon, canonical SMILES lex). For multi-substrate reactions (97% of the corpus) this can pick a conserved cofactor as 'main' when no reaction-center signal is available — NADH/CoA are heavy and win the size contest. No cofactor stripping is applied at this layer.

Cofactor stripping is exact-SMILES-match only. Canonical tautomers, protonation states, or salt forms that differ from the frozenset entry bypass the filter. Deliberately excludes ambiguous co-substrates (2-oxoglutarate/glutamate/pyruvate/acetyl-CoA) which are sometimes the true substrate — correct, but it means _pick_transformed must disambiguate them via reaction center alone.

When per_frag_center is None (chenyu_features unavailable or returns None), it silently degrades to 'largest non-cofactor fragment' — the same size-contest failure mode as pick_main, just with cofactors excluded. The fallback is not flagged in the return value, so callers cannot distinguish a center-anchored pick from a size-based guess.

Returns a SINGLE (X, Y) pair per reaction. The §9.3 canonical case has TWO parallel transformed lineages (proline->hydroxyproline AND 2-oxoglutarate->succinate); legacy can only represent one, forcing a cross-lineage pairing for the other. Also depends on chenyu_features.reaction_center_from_chenyu (imported inside a try/except) — if that import fails, the pair is computed without any reaction-center signal, silently degrading quality.

All three delegate to transformed_pair, so they inherit its single-pair limitation. group_key = (X, Y) means two reactions with the same true transformation but different legacy pairings (due to cofactor/tie ambiguity) land in different groups — splitting a chemical family and inflating apparent diversity.

canon_frags returns a frozenset, discarding stoichiometry and duplicate fragments. This is fine for set-level comparison but means 'spectator' detection (canon_frags(r) & canon_frags(p)) cannot distinguish a truly conserved species from one that appears on both sides with different stoichiometry.

proline_2og_case.note: Located by exact stereo-independent participant structures, not by molecule-name keywords. Reacting-center pairs support fragment lineages but are not represented as full atom mapping.
